source: Open Source Security Testing Methodology Manual 3, ISECOM (https://www.isecom.org)

phases.name: Induction
phases.intent: Establish the truth of the environment: what rules apply, what interference distorts measurement, and whether the target detects interaction at all.

phases.name: Interaction
phases.intent: Measure the attack surface: visibility, access, trust, and the process controls protecting them.

phases.name: Inquest
phases.intent: Measure what the target emanates: processes, configuration, property, segregation, exposure and competitive intelligence.

phases.name: Intervention
phases.intent: Measure what happens under interference: containment, privilege misuse, continuity, and what the target actually recorded.

channels.name: Human Security
channels.scope: People, their interactions, and the psychological and physical means of reaching them.
channels.index: Names, roles, contact points (each person reachable through a channel is a target).

channels.name: Physical Security
channels.scope: Tangible, non-electronic barriers and controls: sites, doors, locks, guards, racks, media, waste.

channels.name: Wireless Communications
channels.scope: All electronic emanation within the scope: 802.11, Bluetooth, RFID/NFC, infrared, cellular, radio, and unintended emissions.
channels.index: BSSIDs/SSIDs, device MACs, tag IDs, frequencies, emitters.

channels.name: Telecommunications
channels.scope: Voice and telephony networks: PSTN lines, PBX, VoIP, voicemail, fax, conferencing, modems.
channels.index: Numbers, extensions, SIP URIs, trunks, mailboxes.

channels.name: Data Networks
channels.scope: Wired and routed networks, systems, services and applications reachable over them.
channels.index: IP addresses, hostnames, URLs/endpoints, ports and services, accounts.

modules.name: Posture Review
modules.purpose: Establish the culture, rules, regulations, legislation, contracts and policies that govern the scope, and the ones the audit itself must obey.
modules.done_when: Applicable obligations are listed with their source, and any that conflict with the planned tests are resolved or excluded in writing.

channel_notes.human-security: HR policy, acceptable-use and awareness obligations; local law on recording, pretexting and employee privacy.
channel_notes.physical-security: Site rules, fire/safety codes, lease and landlord limits, camera and badge-data retention law.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Spectrum regulation, transmit-power limits, legality of capture and jamming in the jurisdiction.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Wiretap and recording law, carrier terms, emergency-service (911/112) prohibitions on test calls.
channel_notes.data-networks: Provider and cloud test policies, data-protection duties over anything captured, third-party hosting consent.

modules.name: Logistics
modules.purpose: Measure the interference between analyst and target — latency, distance, filtering, geography, language, time of day — so later measurements are not artifacts of the path.
modules.done_when: Vantage points, baseline timings and known distortions are recorded, and the index is reachable from the agreed position.

channel_notes.human-security: Language, time zones, working hours, cultural norms that change how a person responds.
channel_notes.physical-security: Travel, sightlines, weather, lighting, shift patterns of the site.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Distance, antenna and gain, noise floor, obstructions, channel congestion.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Trunk quality, carrier routing, IVR timeouts, call-detail delays.
channel_notes.data-networks: Route and latency baselines, upstream filtering, CDN/WAF interposition, rate limits, NAT and geo-blocking.

modules.name: Active Detection Verification
modules.purpose: Verify the breadth and predictability of the target's detection, logging and response before you rely on stealth or on the target's own records.
modules.done_when: It is known what interaction is detected, how fast, by whom, and whether response is consistent enough to be predicted.

channel_notes.human-security: Whether staff report approaches, to whom, and how quickly the report travels.
channel_notes.physical-security: Guard rounds, camera coverage and review, alarm zones and response time.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Rogue-AP and WIDS detection, deauth alerting, client-side warnings.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Fraud/toll alerting, call-pattern monitoring, voicemail lockout thresholds.
channel_notes.data-networks: IDS/WAF/EDR reaction, blocking thresholds, ticket generation, whether blocks are per-IP, per-session or permanent.

modules.name: Visibility Audit
modules.purpose: Enumerate what of the scope can be seen from the agreed vantage point. Each visible target is a Visibility pore.
modules.done_when: The index is complete and de-duplicated, every entry traceable to how it was discovered, and Visibility is a defensible count.

channel_notes.human-security: People discoverable as reachable targets: directories, org charts, social profiles, conference and vendor lists.
channel_notes.physical-security: Visible entrances, windows, enclosures, equipment and signage identifying assets.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Beaconing and non-beaconing networks, paired devices, tags and emitters detectable in scope.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Live numbers in the block, extensions, mailboxes, fax and modem answers.
channel_notes.data-networks: Live hosts, open ports, services and versions, virtual hosts, endpoints and APIs, cloud assets.

modules.name: Access Verification
modules.purpose: Measure the breadth and depth of interactive access points — every place interaction is possible, authenticated or not. Each is an Access pore.
modules.done_when: Every access point is enumerated with the interaction it permits, and Access is counted per point rather than per system.

channel_notes.human-security: Each channel a person actually answers on: phone, mail, chat, in-person, plus who they will accept requests from.
channel_notes.physical-security: Doors, gates, windows, hatches, ports and drop points that admit interaction.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Associable networks, open pairing, readable/writable tags, receivers that accept input.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Answering endpoints, IVR branches, DISA, voicemail systems, conference bridges.
channel_notes.data-networks: Each service, endpoint, parameter surface, login, upload and admin interface that accepts input.

modules.name: Trust Verification
modules.purpose: Determine where targets accept interaction from each other without authentication. Each such relationship is a Trust pore.
modules.done_when: Trust relationships are mapped between indexed targets and assessed against the trust properties (see references/engagement.md).

channel_notes.human-security: Who is believed without verification: internal callers, vendors, badge-wearers, authority claims.
channel_notes.physical-security: Areas entered without re-authentication once inside, shared keys, tailgating tolerance.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Auto-join profiles, remembered SSIDs, trusted pairings, unauthenticated management frames.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Caller-ID trust, internal-extension privilege, voicemail access from inside the PBX.
channel_notes.data-networks: Allow-listed IPs, host trust, service accounts, SSO/token trust, internal APIs assumed private.

modules.name: Controls Verification
modules.purpose: Measure the use and effectiveness of the five process (Class B) controls: non-repudiation, confidentiality, privacy, integrity, alarm.
modules.done_when: Each process control is counted only where verified working against a specific pore, and flaws in them are recorded as Concerns.

channel_notes.human-security: Identity recording, discretion in handling requests, confidential channels, verification steps, reporting duty.
channel_notes.physical-security: Badge and visitor records, shielding from observation, tamper seals, alarms.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Link encryption, MAC/identifier privacy, frame integrity, rogue alarming.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Call logging and CDR retention, encrypted voice, number privacy, fraud alarms.
channel_notes.data-networks: Audit logging, transport and at-rest encryption, PII minimization, signing/hashing, alerting on abuse.

modules.name: Process Verification
modules.purpose: Test whether the controls found are maintained as documented — due diligence under normal and abnormal conditions, not just on the day of the audit.
modules.done_when: Each claimed process has been exercised or evidenced, and drift between documented and operational state is recorded.

channel_notes.human-security: Whether verification, escalation and reporting procedures are followed when inconvenient.
channel_notes.physical-security: Whether visitor, key-issue and disposal procedures hold during shift change and after hours.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Whether rogue findings are acted on and provisioning follows the standard.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Whether extension, mailbox and trunk changes follow change control.
channel_notes.data-networks: Patch, onboarding/offboarding, backup-restore, certificate renewal and incident procedures under load.

modules.name: Configuration / Training Verification
modules.purpose: Compare the operational state to the intended state: configuration for technical channels, training and awareness for the human channel. Establishes whether controls override operational need or the reverse.
modules.done_when: Defaults, deviations and unmanaged assets are documented against the intended baseline.

channel_notes.human-security: Training content, recency and coverage; what staff actually do versus what training says.
channel_notes.physical-security: Lock grades, door closers, camera aim, safe settings, fire-path overrides.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Cipher suites, WPS/legacy protocols, transmit power, guest isolation, default credentials.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Default and unchanged mailbox PINs, call-forward and DISA settings, unused trunks.
channel_notes.data-networks: Hardening baselines, default credentials and pages, TLS configuration, permissive CORS/headers, exposed debug.

modules.name: Property Validation
modules.purpose: Identify intellectual and physical property within the scope that is breached, misused, unlicensed or illegally held.
modules.done_when: Property held in scope is inventoried against entitlement, and misuse is recorded with evidence rather than assumption.

channel_notes.human-security: Company data on personal accounts and devices, shared credentials, unsanctioned tools.
channel_notes.physical-security: Unlicensed media, unaccounted equipment, documents and disposal-bound material left recoverable.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Unauthorized APs and hotspots, rogue tags and devices carrying company data.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Unauthorized lines, forwarding of business calls to private numbers, unsanctioned conferencing.
channel_notes.data-networks: Unlicensed software, leaked source or keys, shadow-IT services and data holding company property.

modules.name: Segregation Review
modules.purpose: Determine the separation between personal information and business information, and the exposure of personal data within the scope.
modules.done_when: Where PII mixes with business assets is identified, with the pores through which it is reachable.

channel_notes.human-security: Personal details discoverable through work channels; use of personal accounts for business.
channel_notes.physical-security: Personal effects and records in business areas, unsecured HR and medical files.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Personal devices on business networks, device identifiers broadcasting people's movements.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Personal numbers in business directories, voicemail containing personal data.
channel_notes.data-networks: PII in logs, backups, test data, tickets and error messages; cross-tenant or cross-user leakage.

modules.name: Exposure Verification
modules.purpose: Discover freely available information that gives indirect visibility of targets or assets in scope. Each such item is an Exposure limitation.
modules.done_when: Public sources have been searched systematically and each exposure is recorded with its source and what it reveals.

channel_notes.human-security: Staff lists, roles, absences, photographs of badges and screens, recruitment detail.
channel_notes.physical-security: Street and satellite imagery, floor plans, permit filings, vendor case studies.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Public wardriving databases, device registration lookups, FCC/type filings.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Published number ranges, directory entries, leaked call detail.
channel_notes.data-networks: Certificate transparency, DNS and passive DNS, code and config in public repos, paste sites, search-engine indexes, cached errors.

modules.name: Competitive Intelligence Scouting
modules.purpose: Derive, from the scope alone, information of competitive value to the target owner — what an adversary learns about the business by watching its infrastructure.
modules.done_when: Business-impacting inferences are documented with the technical observations that support them.

channel_notes.human-security: Hiring, reorganization and partnership signals from people's public activity.
channel_notes.physical-security: Deliveries, expansion works, occupancy and equipment visible from outside.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Vendor fingerprints and device populations revealing platform choices.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Call volumes, IVR menus and site presence revealing operations and scale.
channel_notes.data-networks: Technology stack, third-party dependencies, staging and pre-release assets, growth inferred from infrastructure.

modules.name: Quarantine Verification
modules.purpose: Determine whether hostile or anomalous interaction is contained — in both directions — and how allow/deny decisions are made.
modules.done_when: Containment behaviour is measured for inbound and outbound interaction, including how long it lasts and how it is lifted.

channel_notes.human-security: Whether a suspicious approach is cut off and circulated, or just individually ignored.
channel_notes.physical-security: Mantraps, holding areas, escort rules, whether an unbadged person is stopped rather than merely noticed.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Client isolation, rogue containment, deauth of unknown devices, guest segmentation.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Call blocking, mailbox lockout, fraud cut-off, whether blocks persist.
channel_notes.data-networks: Segmentation and egress filtering, WAF/EDR blocking duration, session invalidation, account lockout.

modules.name: Privileges Audit
modules.purpose: Map credentials and privilege levels and measure the impact of their misuse — including escalation that was never earned.
modules.done_when: Privilege boundaries are tested from each authenticated position available, and every crossing is evidenced.

channel_notes.human-security: What a person will do for a claimed authority; what access an ordinary role can obtain by asking.
channel_notes.physical-security: Where a visitor or contractor badge reaches; master-key and override scope.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Guest-to-internal reachability, management-interface access from the air.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Extension-to-admin functions, DISA to outbound trunks, mailbox-to-mailbox access.
channel_notes.data-networks: Horizontal and vertical access control, token and role handling, admin surface, service-account reach.

modules.name: Survivability Validation / Service Continuity
modules.purpose: Measure the target's resilience to excessive, adverse or interrupted conditions — continuity, failover and graceful failure. Requires explicit written sign-off; skip the module and say so if it is not granted.
modules.done_when: Either resilience is measured within the authorized envelope, or the module is recorded as excluded with the reason.

channel_notes.human-security: Cover during absence, single points of human failure, whether a refused request has a documented fallback.
channel_notes.physical-security: Power, cooling, access during outage, whether fail-safe means open or locked.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: Behaviour under interference and congestion, fallback to weaker modes.
channel_notes.telecommunications: Trunk failover, behaviour when lines saturate, emergency routing (never test live emergency services).
channel_notes.data-networks: Failover and degradation under load, dependency failure handling, backup restore, rate-limit behaviour.

modules.name: Alert and Log Review
modules.purpose: Compare the audit's own record of activity to what the target detected and recorded. The end survey: what really got seen.
modules.done_when: The analyst timeline is reconciled against the target's logs and alerts, and every gap or discrepancy is reported.

channel_notes.human-security: Which approaches were reported, by whom, how accurately, and what was done with the report.
channel_notes.physical-security: Guard logs, visitor books, badge and camera records against the actual visits.
channel_notes.wireless-communications: WIDS and controller logs against the associations and captures performed.
channel_notes.telecommunications: CDRs and fraud alerts against the calls placed.
channel_notes.data-networks: IDS/WAF/EDR/application logs against the requests sent, including what was silently dropped.
